articles.title: Pressure on landlord costs increase as Renters’ Rights Act looms
articles.summary: The average landlord is now carrying £714,000 in borrowing and paying around £25,000 a year in interest alone, before tax, maintenance or compliance costs are taken into account, according to new analysis from Pepper Money and Pegasus Insights.
articles.ai_summary:
- UK landlords face escalating financial pressure with average borrowings hitting £714,000 and annual interest costs reaching £25,000, excluding additional expenses.  
- The looming Renters’ Rights Act intensifies concerns for landlords amidst rising operational costs and regulatory compliance.

articles.title: Wave of last-minute instructions as landlords exit ahead of RRA
articles.summary: With the Renters’ Rights Act coming into force this Friday, Kent and London law firm Thackray Williams says it has had a wave of last-minute instructions from landlords looking to exit the market.
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords are rushing to exit the rental market ahead of the Renters' Rights Act implementation this Friday, prompting a surge in last-minute instructions to law firms.  
- Kent and London-based Thackray Williams reports a significant spike in queries from landlords seeking to divest before the new regulations take effect.

articles.title: Chief property ombudsman welcomes RRA but says landlords need support
articles.summary: The UK’s chief property ombudsman Lesley Horton has said she welcomes the reforms coming with the Renters’ Right Act implementation this week but says that small-scale landlords in particular will need support to adapt to the changes.
articles.ai_summary:
- Chief Property Ombudsman Lesley Horton endorses the upcoming Renters' Right Act reforms while highlighting the need for support for small-scale landlords to navigate the changes.  
- The implementation of the Renters' Right Act this week marks a significant shift in UK rental regulations, aiming to enhance tenant rights.

articles.title: Nervous landlords prompt tenfold rise in instructions, says agent
articles.summary: North-east residential lettings agency Xenia Lettings says it has seen a tenfold rise in instructions from property owners since the start of 2026 as private landlords seek expert help to navigate the Renters’ Rights Act, the biggest phase of which goes live on Friday.
articles.ai_summary:
- Xenia Lettings reports a tenfold increase in property owner instructions as landlords seek guidance on the upcoming Renters’ Rights Act changes.
- The surge reflects growing concerns among landlords about adapting to the major legislative shifts set to take effect this Friday.

articles.title: Accidental landlords warned over Renters Rights Act
articles.summary: “Accidental landlords” could find themselves breaking the law from 1 May, a Warwickshire law firm is warning.
articles.ai_summary:
- Accidental landlords in the UK must brace for potential legal issues starting May 1, as new regulations under the Renters Rights Act come into effect.  
- A Warwickshire law firm cautions that these landlords could accidentally violate rental laws, emphasizing the need for awareness and compliance.

articles.title: Reeves reported to be considering rent controls
articles.summary: Chancellor Rachel Reeves is reported to be thinking about imposing rent controls on Private Rented Sector landlords as part of a range of measures to limit the impact of the Iran War on household finances.
articles.ai_summary:
- Chancellor Rachel Reeves is exploring the implementation of rent controls on private landlords to mitigate the financial impact of the Iran War on households.  
- This initiative is part of a broader set of measures aimed at alleviating economic pressures on UK residents.

articles.title: HMRC increases scrutiny of residential valuations
articles.summary: HMRC is increasingly challenging residential property valuations in inheritance tax (IHT) returns, with the number of cases referred to the Valuation Office Agency (VOA) rising 23.5% in the last year, according to research from TWM Solicitors, a private wealth and family law firm.
articles.ai_summary:
- HMRC boosts scrutiny of residential property valuations for inheritance tax, with referrals to the Valuation Office Agency increasing by 23.5% over the past year.
- TWM Solicitors highlights growing challenges in IHT returns as HMRC intensifies its evaluations.

articles.title: Landlords urged to carry out more detailed pre-purchase checks after RRA
articles.summary: Landlords investing in new rental properties should carry out more detailed pre‑purchase checks to better protect themselves once the Renters’ Rights Act comes into force on 1 May.
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords are advised to conduct thorough pre-purchase checks on rental properties ahead of the Renters’ Rights Act implementation on May 1.  
- Enhanced due diligence is crucial for safeguarding landlords’ interests in light of upcoming regulatory changes.

articles.title: Most landlords to be stricter choosing tenants – survey
articles.summary: A quarter of landlords plan to exit the market as a result of the Renters’ Rights Act, while 60% of those who remain intend to get stricter with tenant vetting, according to a survey of 900 landlords by LegalforLandlords.
articles.ai_summary:
- A quarter of UK landlords are considering leaving the market due to the new Renters’ Rights Act.  
- Among those staying, 60% will implement stricter tenant vetting procedures.

articles.title: Maintenance expert shares top Spring tips to cut costs
articles.summary: Landlords should take advantage of Spring to tackle the underlying cause of issues that might have developed over winter and complying with their increased responsibilities under the Renters’ Rights Act.
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords can save money this Spring by addressing winter-related maintenance issues early, ensuring properties are in top condition.  
- Compliance with the new Renters’ Rights Act is crucial, making timely maintenance even more essential for landlords.

articles.title: Pressure on rents to continue despite halving house price growth forecast
articles.summary: Knight Frank has halved its near-term house price growth forecast to 1.5% for 2026 and lowered itsrental forecasts marginally, due to the economic impacts of conflict in the Middle East.
articles.ai_summary:
- Knight Frank has cut its house price growth forecast to just 1.5% by 2026, reflecting economic uncertainty from the Middle East conflict.  
- Despite this adjustment, rental pressures are expected to persist as demand remains high.

articles.title: Four in five landlords unprepared for Renters’ Right Act
articles.summary: Four in five landlords (82%) are concerned about the impact of the Renters’ Rights Act, with one in two (44%) very concerned. Meanwhile, three-quarters (75%) of landlords say regulation has made them less likely to grow their portfolios, and half (49%) are planning to sell or reduce their stake within two months.
articles.ai_summary:
- **Landlord Anxiety**: 82% of landlords are worried about the Renters’ Rights Act, with nearly half (44%) expressing significant concern.
- **Portfolio Impact**: 75% feel regulations discourage portfolio growth, and 49% plan to sell or reduce their holdings within the next two months.

articles.title: Energy efficiency and EPC ratings become higher focus for tenants
articles.summary: Landlords must consider how to improve EPC ratings to attract tenants, even ahead of the new requirement to upgrade rental properties to a C rating by 2030. It comes as energy efficiency of properties has gained even greater focus as tenants look to save money after the energy price hikes caused by the Iran War.
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords are urged to enhance EPC ratings to attract tenants, as a new requirement mandates rental properties to reach a C rating by 2030.  
- With rising energy costs driven by the Iran War, tenants are prioritizing energy efficiency to reduce their bills.

articles.title: Planning reform fails to inspire confidence – Landbay
articles.summary: Fewer than a quarter of the UK’s landlords feel planning reform will positively impact their business.
articles.ai_summary:
- Only 24% of UK landlords believe planning reform will benefit their business, sparking concerns about confidence in the property market.  
- Landbay highlights pervasive skepticism among landlords regarding the effectiveness of proposed planning changes.

articles.title: Landlords warned a hidden leak could cost thousands
articles.summary: With more than half (58%) of hidden leaks originating outside a property, landlords must remember to focus on the maintenance of pipework outside as well as inside the property, leak detection specialist Aspect has warned.
articles.ai_summary:
- Over 58% of hidden leaks in rental properties start outside, highlighting the need for landlords to prioritize exterior pipework maintenance.  
- Neglecting outdoor plumbing can lead to costly repairs, with leak detection specialists urging proactive measures.

articles.title: As RRA deadline looms, 5 top tips for landlords
articles.summary: From 1 May 2026, the Renters’ Rights Act will implement some of the biggest changes to the Private Rented Sector in England and Wales. The Act will aim to balance landlord and tenant rights and will impose new requirements and regulatory oversight on landlords.
articles.ai_summary:
- Starting May 1, 2026, the Renters’ Rights Act will introduce significant reforms to the Private Rented Sector in England and Wales, enhancing protections for tenants.  
- Landlords must prepare for increased regulations and new obligations to ensure compliance with the upcoming changes.

articles.title: 84% of landlords not ready for RRA – survey
articles.summary: More than eight in ten (84%) of landlords are unprepared for the Renters’ Rights Act go-live on May 1, with 58% at high risk of non-compliance according to new figures.
articles.ai_summary:
- **Majority Unprepared**: 84% of landlords are not ready for the implementation of the Renters’ Rights Act on May 1.  
- **Compliance Concerns**: 58% of landlords face a high risk of non-compliance with the new regulations.

articles.title: Expansion no longer default response to rising demand as rental growth slows
articles.summary: Landlords are restructuring portfolios and financing in response to changing rental demand, rather than focusing on expansion, with the ONS announcement of a slowing in rental growth showing the need to ensure portfolios are right.
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords are shifting strategies from expansion to restructuring portfolios and financing to adapt to changing rental demand.
- Recent ONS data indicates slowing rental growth, highlighting the importance of optimizing existing property investments.

articles.title: Landlords blamed for pushing first-time and local buyers out

articles.ai_summary:

- The findings highlight rising concerns over housing accessibility for new entrants amid increasing investment-driven competition.

articles.title: Next government must stem landlord flow
articles.summary: Scotland's landlords have called for the next Scottish Government to formally recognise the private rented sector's (PRS) importance with a dedicated strategy.
articles.ai_summary:
- Scottish landlords urge the next government to acknowledge the vital role of the private rented sector (PRS) with a focused strategy.  
- There is increasing pressure to address the declining landlord presence in Scotland to ensure stability in the rental market.
